changes: Each agent's Home tab shows what it is doing now, its last actions and the title of each task; the Overview card says what it is working on.
Heartbeats and scheduled runs show as Scheduled on the timeline and no longer count as tasks.
Meeting instructions are now written on the agent's Meetings tab in the console, and each change is confirmed with a code from your firewall.
Each agent's Home tab shows its CPU and memory over time, its activity of the last 12 hours, and a few counts.
The Brain page has an Overview with how many pages the brain keeps, by type, and which agents use it.
Team chat has an Overview with how many messages people and agents sent, and in which channels.
A request to email someone new can now be answered with "Always allow this recipient for this mailbox", confirmed with a code.
When an email waits for your approval, the agent is told why, with the request and the recipients, also on Gmail.
Agents can check whether their request was approved, denied, expired or revoked.
On your firewall's Content rules page, Back to console now opens your Messages rules.
Content rules can now be written as a sentence, such as "Don't share salaries", and the firewall's AI checks every message against it, in chat, email, websites, webhooks, meetings and calls.
When the AI check cannot run, messages a stop or hold rule covers are stopped, and the person writing is asked to send again later.
Content rules: your organization can stop or hold messages your agents send or receive on Telegram, Slack, email, websites, webhooks and team chat.
Content rules also cover meetings and calls: a blocked question never reaches your agent, and a blocked answer is not spoken.
Held and stopped messages are listed on your firewall's own page, with their text kept on the firewall.
In meetings, follow-up requests to a task are no longer dropped after the agent's acknowledgement.
In meetings, the agent always acknowledges a request with a short word before it works on it.
A follow-up to a task started in a meeting now continues that task, with what it did so far.
Meeting lookups no longer repeat their instructions each time, so they stay small in long meetings.
HTML widgets and pages the agent makes now open in its dashboard. Only signed-in members of the organization can see them.
In meetings, the agent's lookups now carry only what was said since its last answer, so they stay small in long meetings.
Groundwork for showing HTML widgets in the dashboard, signed in like the dashboard itself (not turned on yet).
Meetings: the agent's lookups run on a fast model you can choose in its Meetings settings, so it answers sooner.
Meetings: the agent no longer comments on the conversation by itself, opens and shows a page when asked to show a site, can browse during a meeting, and leaves when asked.
Security: optional content rules on the firewall stop, hold for approval or record Telegram messages that match them; leaking secrets is always checked. Every change needs a confirmation code.
Meetings: the agent answers questions in a meeting faster, on a fast model you can choose in its Meetings settings.
Meetings: the agent leaves a meeting when someone asks it to, and presents its screen only when it was asked directly.
Meetings: an owner can let the agent present its browser in a meeting (confirmed with a code); ask it to share its screen or stop.
Meetings: each meeting's page links every session the agent ran for it to that session in the agent's dashboard.
Agents on the included AI tokens reuse their cached prompt between replies, so Claude models answer faster and cost less.
Meetings: an owner can let the agent do real work when asked in a meeting (Full agent), confirmed with a code; it says "ok, on it" and tells the room the result.
Meetings: the agent answers only when it is sure it was addressed, says a short "ok" before it looks something up, and keeps its answers shorter.
Confirmation codes sent on Telegram have number buttons: tap the number your console shows instead of typing the code.
When you replace the organization's recovery key, every agent's disk is re-sealed to the new key, and you are told once the old key is no longer needed.
Email rules: a new outgoing mode, Send to anyone, lets your agents email any address without asking you, up to your hourly and daily limits. Switching to it needs a confirmation code.
An agent that takes a long time to start, for example after AgentMail is set up, is no longer restarted while it starts.
Shared notes: your organization's notes now reach your agents, are kept inside each agent's encrypted disk, and your agents search them.
Add storage: you can make an agent's own storage larger from its page while it runs.
A new agent's page says Pairing its disk until your firewall can open it, and asks before a restart that would leave the disk locked.
After applying a template you can test the agent, let Doctor fix a step that failed, and let an AI write the steps Save as template cannot read.
Templates can add scheduled messages and MCP servers, and can use bundles; a bundle can also be applied to an agent that already runs.
Skills and shared notes can be installed, updated and removed on agents that already run, with one confirmation code for several agents.
A skill an agent wrote can be saved into your organization's skills.
Code messages from your firewall say what is asked on the first line and show the code on the second.
An Update no longer fails or waits when Google's download servers for Chrome are slow.
Update your firewall before your agents. Update everything does this in the right order.
Applying a template to an agent that is already running now asks for a confirmation code from your chat channel.
Code messages from your firewall now show the code and the firewall's own facts first, and any text typed in the console separately below.
Each request your firewall sends to an agent now works once and only for that agent, so a copied request cannot be reused.
New agents start with the skills your organization marks for them on the Skills page.
Update your firewall before your agents: an updated agent does not accept requests from an older firewall. Update everything does this in the right order.
An agent's page has a Skills tab: what it has, where each skill came from, and a switch for each.
A template can carry skills, and you can save an agent's setup as a template of your own.
The agent page shows CPU, memory and disk use.
When you apply a template to an agent that already has instructions, you can review and edit them on the agent.
The disk figure now reads the way df does, and the fuller of the server's disk and the agent's own storage is shown.
Your organization can keep its own agent templates and create or set up agents from them.
A template's file steps write only inside the agent's workspace; anything else is a script you can read before confirming.
A template can be applied to an agent that already runs: you see what would change first, then confirm once.
Agent templates: a new agent can start as a Personal assistant, Software factory, Chief of staff or Support agent, set up for you when it is created.
The agent page lists what is left for you to connect after a template, and ticks items off as you do them.
Agent templates, first part: an agent can be set up from one template file with cc-runbook. Nothing in the console uses it yet.
Signing in to Google with a saved login works again; it was blocked by mistake in 1.4.3.
A request that asks the site to treat it as a different kind of request never gets a saved password, and the firewall's login page explains what a sign-in address must be.
A saved website password is now put in only at the site's sign-in, in the password field. A login needs its sign-in page, and anything else that carries the stand-in is blocked.
Meeting notes are written on an agent that has a mailbox, and a failed notes run is tried again later.
An agent no longer freezes during heavy web research: it can hold many more connections, and it recovers by itself if it gets stuck.

Meetings: the agent can listen the whole time without a wake word, set reminders when asked, join from calendar invites, join signed in to its Google account, and act on a meeting afterwards by your instructions.
Your firewall's pages (Logs, Doctor, Website logins) have the ControlClaw look, and the page an agent sends you to add a login works well on a phone.
Screenshots of a browser tab that is not in front no longer time out, and unused search providers are switched off.
Wake chimes in meetings are louder and play at a steady level.
Wake chimes in meetings are now heard: the agent's microphone no longer turns them down.
Doctor offers a list of current models, starting on GPT-6.1 Sol, and opens with the agent you came from.
Each agent's pages have a Doctor link, and the firewall's Logs page links to Doctor.
Website logins work with short passwords and PINs, HTTP sign-in prompts and XML forms.
The login alarm no longer blocks pages by mistake, and a password a site shows back is hidden from the agent.
Website logins: save logins on the firewall, and your agents sign in to sites without ever seeing the password.
Your agent can ask you for a login with a secure link instead of in chat, and handles two-step codes.
Firewall Doctor repairs the firewall itself, even when its pages are down.
Doctor works when an agent's management service is down, and can be started from the firewall.
The firewall no longer fills its log with thousands of disk-key checks.
Changing or removing a fallback model works, and a change the agent refuses now says so.
The health check no longer fails on slow ChatGPT models, and shows OpenClaw status unknown instead of stopped.
Firewall Logs loads on older firewalls, and says when the firewall needs an update.
Your firewall has a Logs page that shows each of its services and the last update.
Download workspace saves a readable copy of your agent: its files, memory, conversations, meetings and calls.
Meetings join again after the latest OpenClaw update, and a failed join now says why.
The Doctor tab shows a quick health status and a Check that finds problems and suggests fixes.
Agent pages share one look with a Back to console button, and Meetings has a new list and a page for each meeting.
Agents and firewalls show a version number and what changed in each update.
First numbered release: agents and firewalls now show a version instead of a build code.
